```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
library(zufuzz)
```

Most R packages that matter to a fuzzer have C or C++ underneath. A fuzzer on
its own only notices a native bug when the process actually dies, and the
memory-safety bugs worth finding usually do not die at the point of the
defect. They corrupt something and carry on, and the crash — if it comes at
all — happens somewhere else, on a later input, in unrelated code.

A sanitizer closes that gap. It turns "wrote four bytes past the end of a
buffer" into a report and an immediate death, at the line responsible.

**zufuzz never owns a sanitizer.** It orchestrates processes that have one,
reads the reports they leave behind, and tells you when a run you believed was
sanitized was not. That is the same split Atheris and Ruzzy make.

## Three separate capabilities

Keeping these apart explains why some of this works everywhere and some of it
does not.

| Capability | Who provides it | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Catching a native crash and saving the input | the engine's signal handling | nothing |
| Detecting memory-safety and UB bugs that do not crash | the ASan/UBSan runtime compiled into the target | a sanitized build |
| Native coverage feedback | Clang SanitizerCoverage, delivered to an in-process engine | the companion package |

The first is always available. The second is what this vignette is about. The
third is not in 0.1.0.

## The recommended configuration

Run `afl-fuzz` over an R that is itself a sanitized build. The R process that
runs your target is an ordinary child of the supervisor, the sanitizer runtime
is simply present, and nothing has to be preloaded or injected.

Community images that already have this:

- `rocker/r-devel-san` — GCC, ASan + UBSan
- `rocker/r-devel-ubsan-clang` — Clang, UBSan
- `wch1/r-debug` — supplies `RDsan` and `RDcsan` binaries

Install your target package *inside* the image, so it is compiled with the
same instrumentation, then run the campaign as usual:

```sh
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:alloc_dealloc_mismatch=0:allocator_may_return_null=1:abort_on_error=1 \
UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1:halt_on_error=1 \
afl-fuzz -i corpus -o out -- Rscript harness.R
```

`zufuzz::sanitizer_options()` returns those two strings, so you can pass them
to a child rather than retyping them:

```r
fuzz_file("harness.R", corpus = "corpus", engine = "afl",
          env = sanitizer_options())
```

### Why each option

None of these are stylistic; a campaign misbehaves without them.

- **`detect_leaks=0`** — R deliberately leaves allocations for the OS to
  reclaim at exit. With leak detection on, every run ends in a leak report,
  and real findings are buried under them. A leak report from a zufuzz run
  therefore means this option did not reach the process, and zufuzz reports it
  as a configuration fault rather than as a finding.
- **`allocator_may_return_null=1`** — lets a huge allocation reach R's own
  out-of-memory path, where it becomes an R error. Without it ASan aborts and
  you get a "finding" that is really the fuzzer asking for 2 GB.
- **`abort_on_error=1`** — makes a report end in `SIGABRT`. This one is
  load-bearing: without it ASan exits with status 1, and a supervisor watching
  for a crash records *nothing at all*. The campaign looks clean.
- **`halt_on_error=1`** — UBSan otherwise prints and continues, so the input
  that caused it is long gone by the time anything notices.

## Check that it took effect

The failure worth designing against is a sanitized campaign that quietly was
not one: it finds fewer bugs, exits zero, and looks exactly like a clean run.

```r
sanitizer_status()
#> <zufuzz sanitizer status>
#>   sanitized (asan)
#>    - runtime mapped into this process: asan
```

`sanitized` is `TRUE` only when the runtime is actually mapped into the
process — read from `/proc/self/maps`. Build flags and `LD_PRELOAD` are
reported as evidence but never counted as proof: they say what was asked for,
not what happened. On platforms with no `/proc`, the status says `unknown`
rather than guessing in either direction.

## What a native finding looks like

A sanitizer abort kills the process outright, so no R code runs afterwards and
there is no R condition to record. zufuzz rebuilds the finding from the log:

```r
res <- replay("harness.R", "crash-9c1185a5...")
res$outcome
#> [1] "sanitizer"
res$native$category
#> [1] "heap-buffer-overflow"
res$native$top_frames
#> [1] "zujson_decode_utf8 utf8.c:204" "zujson_parse parse.c:77"
```

Two details in `top_frames` are deliberate. The sanitizer's own interceptors
are dropped — frame #0 of a heap overflow is `__asan_memcpy`, which is true
and tells you nothing — and so are R's evaluator frames, which appear in
every finding and so cannot tell two bugs apart.

The fingerprint is the kind, the category, and the top frame that belongs to
your code. Not the address, the pid, the shadow bytes, or the build directory:
those change between runs of the same defect, and a fingerprint that follows
them would match nothing and gate nothing.

## Findings that cannot be minimized

`minimize()` refuses two kinds of native finding, and the refusal is the
correct answer rather than a limitation:

- **A bare signal with no report.** Nothing describes the defect, so a smaller
  input that also dies cannot be shown to die of the *same* thing. Both
  `afl-tmin` and libFuzzer's `-minimize_crash` will happily shrink one crash
  into a different one and report success; zufuzz will not. Re-run under a
  sanitized build to get a report worth shrinking.
- **A leak report**, which means the options above did not take effect.

The artifact is still saved in both cases. It is a real input that killed a
real process, and it is worth keeping.

## What sanitizers will not catch in R

- **Missing `PROTECT` and premature GC.** Not memory-unsafe from ASan's point
  of view — the memory is still mapped and still valid; it is just no longer
  yours. Use `fuzz(gc_torture = TRUE)` as the complement, and `rchk` for
  static checking.
- **Deep recursion in R code**, which surfaces as R's "C stack usage" error.
- **R API misuse** such as passing the wrong `SEXP` type, which R's own checks
  usually report as an ordinary R error — already a finding.

## Platforms

| | Linux | macOS | Windows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sanitized R build + AFL++ | yes, recommended | untested | no |
| Runtime detection | yes | reports `unknown` | reports `unknown` |
| Reading a report someone else captured | yes | yes | yes |

Parsing, fingerprinting and refusing to minimize are pure R and work
everywhere, including on a report captured on another machine.

Stock R plus a sanitized target package — which needs the runtime preloaded
ahead of R, the way Atheris ships `asan_with_fuzzer.so` — is **not available
in 0.1.0**. It requires the in-process companion engine, and
`preload_path()` arrives with it.
